units.zh: 劉裕進據鄭城。
units.en: Liu Yu took Zheng.
units.literal: Liu Yu advanced and occupied Zheng city.

units.zh: 泓使姚裕、尚書龐統屯兵宮中，姚洸屯於灃西，尚書姚白瓜徙四軍雜戶入長安，姚丕守渭橋，胡翼度屯石積，姚贊屯霸東，泓軍於逍遙園。
units.en: Yao Hong sent Yao Yu and the minister Pang Tong to station troops in the palace, Yao Guang to garrison west of Feng, the minister Yao Baigua to move the mixed households of the four armies into Chang'an, Yao Pi to guard the Wei Bridge, Hu Yidu to garrison Shiji, Yao Zan to garrison east of the Ba, while Hong himself encamped at Xiaoyao Garden.
units.literal: Hong sent Yao Yu and Minister Pang Tong to camp troops in the palace, Yao Guang west of the Feng, Minister Yao Baigua moved four-army miscellaneous households into Chang'an, Yao Pi guarded Wei Bridge, Hu Yidu camped at Stone Accumulation, Yao Zan east of Ba; Hong encamped at Free-Roam Garden.

value.statement: moved the mixed households of the four armies into Chang'an

units.zh: 鎮惡夾渭進兵，破姚丕於渭橋。
units.en: Wang Zhen'e shattered Yao Pi at the Wei bridge.
units.literal: Zhen'e advanced troops on both sides of the Wei, defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.

proposals.before: Wang Zhen'e shattered Yao Pi at the Wei bridge.
proposals.after: Wang Zhen’e advanced along both banks of the Wei and defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.
proposals.reason: 夾渭 specifies the advance on both banks before the defeat at Wei Bridge.

units.zh: 泓自逍遙園赴之，逼水地狹，因丕之敗，遂相踐而退。
units.en: Yao Hong's relief column stampeded itself in the narrow river flats.
units.literal: Hong went from Free-Roam Garden to aid him; pressed by water, ground narrow, because of Pi's defeat, they trampled each other in retreat.

proposals.before: Yao Hong's relief column stampeded itself in the narrow river flats.
proposals.after: Yao Hong came from Xiaoyao Garden to help Yao Pi. The ground was narrow against the river, and when Pi was defeated the men trampled one another as they retreated.
proposals.reason: Restore Hong’s point of departure, his attempt to aid Pi, Pi’s defeat, and the trampling in retreat.

units.zh: 姚諶及前軍姚烈、左衛姚寶安、散騎王帛、建武姚進、揚威姚蠔、尚書右丞孫玄等皆死於陣，泓單馬還宮。
units.en: Yao Chen; Yao Lie of the Vanguard; Yao Bao'an of the Left Guard; Cavalier Attendant Wang Bo; General Who Establishes Martial Might Yao Jin; General Who Displays Might Yao Hao; Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Sun Xuan; and the others all died in battle. Yao Hong rode back to the palace alone.
units.literal: Yao Chen and forward army Yao Lie, left guard Yao Bao'an, supernumerary Wang Bo, Jianwei Yao Jin, General Who Displays Might Yao Hao, right aide Sun Xuan and others all died in formation; Hong alone on horseback returned to the palace.

proposals.before: Yao Chen and forward army Yao Lie, left guard Yao Bao'an, supernumerary Wang Bo, Jianwei Yao Jin, General Who Displays Might Yao Hao, right aide Sun Xuan and others all died in formation; Hong alone on horseback returned to the palace.
proposals.after: Yao Chen, Yao Lie of the Vanguard, Yao Bao’an of the Left Guard, Cavalier Attendant Wang Bo, Yao Jin, General Who Establishes Martial Might, Yao Hao, General Who Displays Might, Sun Xuan, right assistant director of the Department of State Affairs, and others all died in battle. Hong returned to the palace alone on horseback.
proposals.reason: 建武 is Jianwu, not Jianwei. Restore Sun Xuan’s department and the military and court designations of the fallen.

value.en: Right Aide of the Masters of Writing

label.en: Right Aide of the Masters of Writing

units.zh: 鎮惡入自平朔門，泓與姚裕等數百騎出奔于石橋。
units.en: Wang Zhen'e broke Pingshuo Gate; Yao Hong fled toward Stone Bridge.
units.literal: Zhen'e entered from Pingshuo Gate; Hong with Yao Yu and several hundred horse fled out toward Stone Bridge.

proposals.before: Wang Zhen'e broke Pingshuo Gate; Yao Hong fled toward Stone Bridge.
proposals.after: Wang Zhen’e entered through Pingshuo Gate. Yao Hong, Yao Yu and the others fled with several hundred horsemen to Stone Bridge.
proposals.reason: Zhen’e entered through the gate; no breaking of the gate is reported. Restore Yao Yu and the several hundred horsemen fleeing with Hong.

units.zh: 贊聞泓之敗也，召將士告之，眾皆以刀擊地，攘袂大泣。
units.en: Yao Zan's men wept and beat the ground when they heard the news.
units.literal: When Zan heard of Hong's defeat, he summoned officers and soldiers and told them; all struck the earth with knives, pulled sleeves and wept greatly.

proposals.before: Yao Zan's men wept and beat the ground when they heard the news.
proposals.after: When Yao Zan learned of Hong’s defeat, he summoned his officers and men and told them. They all struck the ground with their knives, pushed up their sleeves and wept aloud.
proposals.reason: Restore Zan as recipient and messenger of the news, the knives, the sleeve gesture and the loud weeping.

units.zh: 胡翼度先與劉裕陰通，是日棄眾奔裕。
units.en: Hu Yidu defected to Liu Yu.
units.literal: Hu Yidu had earlier secretly communicated with Liu Yu; that day he abandoned the host and fled to Yu.

proposals.before: Hu Yidu defected to Liu Yu.
proposals.after: Hu Yidu had already been in secret contact with Liu Yu. That day he abandoned his men and fled to Yu.
proposals.reason: Hu Yidu had already been in secret contact with Liu Yu and deserted his troops that day.

units.zh: 贊夜率諸軍，將會泓于石橋，王師已固諸門，贊軍不得入，眾皆驚散。
units.en: Yao Zan could not re-enter the sealed capital.
units.literal: Zan by night led all armies, planning to join Hong at Stone Bridge; the royal army had already secured all gates; Zan's army could not enter; the host all startled and scattered.

proposals.before: Yao Zan could not re-enter the sealed capital.
proposals.after: That night Yao Zan led the armies out to join Hong at Stone Bridge. The Jin army already held all the gates. Zan’s army could not enter, and his men scattered in alarm.
proposals.reason: Restore Zan’s night march to meet Hong at Stone Bridge, Jin’s control of the gates and his men’s dispersal.

units.zh: 泓計無所出，謀欲降於裕。
units.en: Yao Hong decided to surrender to Liu Yu.
units.literal: Hong had no plan left, plotted wishing to surrender to Yu.

proposals.before: Yao Hong decided to surrender to Liu Yu.
proposals.after: At a loss for any other plan, Yao Hong considered surrendering to Liu Yu.
proposals.reason: Restore Hong’s inability to devise any other plan and his deliberation about surrender.

units.zh: 其子佛念，年十一，謂泓曰：「晉人將逞其欲，終必不全，願自裁決。」
units.en: His eleven-year-old son Yao Fonian said: "Surrender will not save us—better to die cleanly."
units.literal: His son Fonian, age eleven, said to Hong, "The Jin people will indulge their desires to the end—you will surely not be preserved whole; I wish to decide for myself."

proposals.before: His eleven-year-old son Yao Fonian said: "Surrender will not save us—better to die cleanly."
proposals.after: His eleven-year-old son Fonian said to Hong, “The Jin men will have their way, and in the end they surely will not spare you. I beg you to take your own life.”
proposals.reason: The eleven-year-old addresses Hong, warning that Jin will have its way and will not spare him. 願自裁決 urges suicide, not permission to decide for the child. The parallel in Zizhi tongjian 118 reads 不如引決 and Hu Sanxing glosses it as 自裁.

proposals.before: His son Fonian, age eleven, said to Hong, "The Jin people will indulge their desires to the end—you will surely not be preserved whole; I wish to decide for myself."
proposals.after: His eleven-year-old son Fonian said to Hong, “The Jin men will have their way, and in the end they surely will not spare you. I beg you to take your own life.”
proposals.reason: The eleven-year-old addresses Hong, warning that Jin will have its way and will not spare him. 願自裁決 urges suicide, not permission to decide for the child. The parallel in Zizhi tongjian 118 reads 不如引決 and Hu Sanxing glosses it as 自裁.

units.zh: 泓憮然不答。
units.en: Yao Hong could not answer.
units.literal: Hong looked mournful and did not answer.

proposals.before: Yao Hong could not answer.
proposals.after: Yao Hong was stricken and gave no answer.
proposals.reason: 憮然 describes Hong’s distress; 不答 says he did not answer, not that he was unable.

units.zh: 佛念遂登宮牆自投而死。
units.en: Yao Fonian leaped from the palace wall.
units.literal: Fonian then climbed the palace wall and threw himself down to die.

proposals.before: Yao Fonian leaped from the palace wall.
proposals.after: Yao Fonian then climbed the palace wall and threw himself to his death.
proposals.reason: Restore climbing the wall and dying of his deliberate fall.

value.manner: suicide by throwing himself from the palace wall

units.zh: 泓將妻子詣壘門而降。
units.en: Yao Hong brought his family to Liu Yu's camp and yielded.
units.literal: Hong led wife and children to the camp gate and surrendered.

proposals.before: Yao Hong brought his family to Liu Yu's camp and yielded.
proposals.after: Yao Hong took his wife and children to the gate of Liu Yu’s camp and surrendered.
proposals.reason: 妻子 explicitly identifies his wife and children, and he went to the camp gate.

units.zh: 贊率宗室子弟百餘人亦降於裕，裕盡殺之，余宗遷於江南。
units.en: Liu Yu slaughtered the surrendered Yao princes and deported the clan to the south.
units.literal: Zan led more than a hundred sons and nephews of the imperial clan also to surrender to Yu; Yu killed them all; the rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangzi.

proposals.before: Liu Yu slaughtered the surrendered Yao princes and deported the clan to the south.
proposals.after: Yao Zan also surrendered to Liu Yu, leading more than a hundred younger men of the imperial clan. Liu Yu killed them all. The rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangtze.
proposals.reason: Restore Zan leading over a hundred younger imperial clansmen to surrender, the killing of them all, and the distinct fate of the remaining clan south of the Yangtze.

units.zh: 送泓于建康市斬之，時年三十，在位二年。
units.en: Yao Hong was executed in the Jiankang market at thirty after two years' reign.
units.literal: They sent Hong to Jiankang market and beheaded him; he was thirty years old, on the throne two years.

proposals.before: Yao Hong was executed in the Jiankang market at thirty after two years' reign.
proposals.after: Yao Hong was sent to Jiankang and beheaded in the marketplace. He was thirty years old and had reigned for two years.
proposals.reason: The account describes Hong’s conveyance to Jiankang and execution by beheading specifically.

units.zh: 建康百里之內，草木皆燋死焉。
units.en: Within a hundred li of Jiankang, grass and trees all scorched dead.
units.literal: Within a hundred li of Jiankang, grass and trees all scorched dead.

units.zh: 姚萇以孝武太元九年僭立，至泓三世，以安帝義熙十三年而滅，凡三十二年。
units.en: From Yao Chang's usurpation in the ninth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu to the fall in the thirteenth year of Yixi under Emperor An, the Later Qin lasted three reigns and thirty-two years.
units.literal: Yao Chang presumptuously rose in the ninth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu; down to Hong three generations; in the thirteenth year of Yixi under Emperor An they perished—thirty-two years in all.

units.zh: 史評
units.en: Section heading marking a later historical appraisal.
units.literal: Section heading marking a later historical appraisal.

proposals.before: Section heading marking a later historical appraisal.
proposals.after: Historical Appraisal
proposals.reason: 史評 is the heading itself; translate it instead of describing its editorial function.

proposals.before: Section heading marking a later historical appraisal.
proposals.after: Historical Appraisal
proposals.reason: 史評 is the heading itself; translate it instead of describing its editorial function.

units.zh: 史臣曰：自長江徙禦，化龍創業，巨寇乘機而未寧，戎馬交馳而不息，晦重氛於六漠，鼓洪流於八際，天未厭亂，凶旅實繁。
units.en: The historian opens: age of warlords and tribal armies without end.
units.literal: The historiographer says: From moving the defense to the Yangtze, transforming dragon and founding enterprise, great bandits seized the chance and were not yet quiet; war-horses galloped one upon another without rest; heavy murk veiled the six deserts, great floods drummed the eight bounds—Heaven had not tired of chaos, and fierce hosts were truly many.

proposals.before: The historian opens: age of warlords and tribal armies without end.
proposals.after: The court historian says: Since the imperial court moved to the Yangtze and the prince who became a dragon founded the dynasty there, great raiders have seized their opportunity and never been quiet. Warhorses have galloped back and forth without rest. Thick murk darkened the six reaches of the world, and great floods surged to its eight limits. Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and violent armies were many indeed.
proposals.reason: 徙御 is the removal of the imperial court, not its defense. 化龍 invokes the crossing and accession of Jin’s founder in the south (the rhyme in Jinshu 6). Restore the unrest, the warhorses, darkness, floods, Heaven and the multitude of violent armies.

proposals.before: The historiographer says: From moving the defense to the Yangtze, transforming dragon and founding enterprise, great bandits seized the chance and were not yet quiet; war-horses galloped one upon another without rest; heavy murk veiled the six deserts, great floods drummed the eight bounds—Heaven had not tired of chaos, and fierce hosts were truly many.
proposals.after: The court historian says: Since the imperial court moved to the Yangtze and the prince who became a dragon founded the dynasty there, great raiders have seized their opportunity and never been quiet. Warhorses have galloped back and forth without rest. Thick murk darkened the six reaches of the world, and great floods surged to its eight limits. Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and violent armies were many indeed.
proposals.reason: 徙御 is the removal of the imperial court, not its defense. 化龍 invokes the crossing and accession of Jin’s founder in the south (the rhyme in Jinshu 6). Restore the unrest, the warhorses, darkness, floods, Heaven and the multitude of violent armies.

units.zh: 弋仲越自金方，言歸石氏，抗直詞於暴主，闡忠訓于危朝，貽厥之謀，在乎歸順，鳴哀之義，有足稱焉。
units.en: Yao Yizhong defied Shi Hu yet sought peace—his loyalty earns praise.
units.literal: Yizhong crossed from the metal quarter, spoke of returning to the Shi house, raised straight words to a violent lord, spread loyal instruction in a perilous court—his plan for posterity lay in submission; the meaning of his lament is worth praising.

proposals.before: Yao Yizhong defied Shi Hu yet sought peace—his loyalty earns praise.
proposals.after: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke with uncompromising frankness to a violent ruler and set forth the counsels of loyalty at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.
proposals.reason: 金方 is the west; Yizhong gave allegiance to the Shi and spoke frankly to their violent ruler. His dying counsel was submission to Jin, explicit in Jinshu 116, 我死，汝便歸晉. 鳴哀 evokes his final words.

proposals.before: Yizhong crossed from the metal quarter, spoke of returning to the Shi house, raised straight words to a violent lord, spread loyal instruction in a perilous court—his plan for posterity lay in submission; the meaning of his lament is worth praising.
proposals.after: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke with uncompromising frankness to a violent ruler and set forth the counsels of loyalty at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.
proposals.reason: 金方 is the west; Yizhong gave allegiance to the Shi and spoke frankly to their violent ruler. His dying counsel was submission to Jin, explicit in Jinshu 116, 我死，汝便歸晉. 鳴哀 evokes his final words.

value.assessment: straight speech to a violent lord; loyal instruction; posterity plan in submission; lament worthy of praise

units.zh: 景國弱歲英奇，見方孫策，詳其幹識，無忝斯言，遂踐迷途，良可悲矣！
units.en: Yao Xiang matched Sun Ce in dash but marched into tragedy.
units.literal: Jingguo in weak years was heroic and strange, compared to Sun Ce; examining his capacity and insight, he did not shame that saying—yet he trod a lost road, truly lamentable!

proposals.before: Yao Xiang matched Sun Ce in dash but marched into tragedy.
proposals.after: Yao Xiang, called Jingguo, showed exceptional courage and talent from his youth and was compared to Sun Ce. A close look at his ability and judgment bears out the comparison. That he went on to take a mistaken path is indeed cause for sorrow.
proposals.reason: 景國 identifies Xiang by his courtesy name. Restore the comparison made in his youth, the judgment on his ability and the historian’s lament for his misguided course.

value.assessment: heroic in youth, compared to Sun Ce, then trod a lost road

units.zh: 景茂因仲襄之緒，躡苻亡之會，嘯命群豪，恢弘霸業，假容沖之銳，俯定函、秦；
units.en: Yao Chang took up Yao Xiang's legacy, stepped into Fu Jian's fall, whistled command to the heroes, enlarged the hegemon's enterprise, and borrowed Murong Chong's edge to settle Hangu and Qin.
units.literal: Jingmao took up Zhongxiang's thread, stepped into Fu's fall, whistled command to the heroes, enlarged the hegemon's enterprise—borrowed Chong's edge to bow and settle Han and Qin;

proposals.before: Yao Chang took up Yao Xiang's legacy, stepped into Fu Jian's fall, whistled command to the heroes, enlarged the hegemon's enterprise, and borrowed Murong Chong's edge to settle Hangu and Qin.
proposals.after: Yao Chang, called Jingmao, took up the work left by Yao Yizhong and Yao Xiang. Seizing the occasion of the Fu house’s collapse, he called the regional leaders to his side and extended his dominion. Drawing on the force of Murong Chong’s attack, he secured Hangu and the Qin lands with ease.
proposals.reason: 仲襄 refers jointly to Yizhong and Xiang, father and elder brother of Chang, not a person named Zhongxiang or Xiang alone. 容沖 is Murong Chong. Preserve both named regions in the parallel. Cf. Jinshu 116.

proposals.before: Jingmao took up Zhongxiang's thread, stepped into Fu's fall, whistled command to the heroes, enlarged the hegemon's enterprise—borrowed Chong's edge to bow and settle Han and Qin;
proposals.after: Yao Chang, called Jingmao, took up the work left by Yao Yizhong and Yao Xiang. Seizing the occasion of the Fu house’s collapse, he called the regional leaders to his side and extended his dominion. Drawing on the force of Murong Chong’s attack, he secured Hangu and the Qin lands with ease.
proposals.reason: 仲襄 refers jointly to Yizhong and Xiang, father and elder brother of Chang, not a person named Zhongxiang or Xiang alone. 容沖 is Murong Chong. Preserve both named regions in the parallel. Cf. Jinshu 116.

units.zh: 挫雷惡之鋒，載甯東北。
units.en: He broke Murong Chui's power and quieted the northeast.
units.literal: broke the point of Lei E, brought peace to the northeast.

proposals.before: He broke Murong Chui's power and quieted the northeast.
proposals.after: He blunted Lei Edi’s attack and brought peace to the northeast.
proposals.reason: 雷惡 abbreviates Lei Edi, not Murong Chui; Jinshu 116 places Lei Edi’s attack in the northeast and narrates its defeat.

proposals.before: broke the point of Lei E, brought peace to the northeast.
proposals.after: He blunted Lei Edi’s attack and brought peace to the northeast.
proposals.reason: 雷惡 abbreviates Lei Edi, not Murong Chui; Jinshu 116 places Lei Edi’s attack in the northeast and narrates its defeat.

units.zh: 在茲奸略，實冠凶徒。
units.en: In cunning he outdid every rival warlord.
units.literal: In these crafty stratagems he truly crowned the villains.

value.assessment: crafty stratagems crowned the villains; planted trees to mark camps; unbenevolent toward old lord; lucky to die in bed

units.zh: 列樹而表新營，雖云效績；
units.en: He marked new camps with trees—passing as order.
units.literal: Planting trees to mark new camps—though called achievement;

proposals.before: He marked new camps with trees—passing as order.
proposals.after: The rows of trees that marked his new camp may indeed be called a record of achievement.
proposals.reason: This refers to planting trees to commemorate a military victory at the camp, described in Jinshu 116: 萇命其將當城于營處一柵孔中蒔樹一根，以旌戰功. 效績 concedes an accomplishment.

value.assessment: crafty stratagems crowned the villains; planted trees to mark camps; unbenevolent toward old lord; lucky to die in bed

units.zh: 薦棘而陵舊主，何其不仁！
units.en: Yet he trampled his old lord Fu Jian—heartless.
units.literal: pushing brambles to climb the old lord—how lacking in benevolence!

proposals.before: Yet he trampled his old lord Fu Jian—heartless.
proposals.after: But to lay the body of his former lord Fu Jian on thorns and dishonor him in that way—what cruelty!
proposals.reason: 薦棘 is literally laying the exhumed body of Chang’s former lord Fu Jian on thorns. Jinshu 116 states 萇乃掘苻堅屍 … 薦之以棘. 陵 denotes maltreatment or humiliation.

proposals.after: But to lay the body of his former lord Fu Jian on thorns and dishonor him in that way—what cruelty!

units.zh: 安枕而終，斯為幸也。
units.en: He died in bed—that was luck enough.
units.literal: To pillow in peace and end—this was fortune.

value.assessment: crafty stratagems crowned the villains; planted trees to mark camps; unbenevolent toward old lord; lucky to die in bed

units.zh: 子略克摧勍敵，荷成先構，虛襟訪道，側席求賢，敦友弟以睦其親，明賞罰以臨其下，英髦盡節，爪牙畢命。
units.en: Yao Xing broke strong enemies, finished his father's work, sought wise counsel, knit his clan, and ruled with clear rewards—rivaling Zhuang of Chu or Mu of Qin.
units.literal: Zilue was able to crush mighty foes, bore the completed prior structure, emptied breast to visit the Way, set aside mat to seek worthies, thickly befriended younger brothers to harmonize kin, clarified rewards and punishments to face those below—heroes exhausted their integrity, claws and fangs gave their lives.

proposals.before: Yao Xing broke strong enemies, finished his father's work, sought wise counsel, knit his clan, and ruled with clear rewards—rivaling Zhuang of Chu or Mu of Qin.
proposals.after: Yao Xing, called Zilüe, crushed powerful enemies and carried forward the work his predecessor had begun. With an open mind he sought instruction and made room at his side for worthy men. His affection for his brothers brought harmony to the family, and he governed his subjects by clear rewards and punishments. Men of talent served him with complete devotion, and his fighting men gave their lives for him.
proposals.reason: Restore the full progression through Xing’s predecessor, consultations, recruitment of worthy men, family relationships, paired rewards and punishments, and the loyalty and sacrifice of officers and warriors. The comparison with Chu and Qin belongs to s0261.

proposals.before: Zilue was able to crush mighty foes, bore the completed prior structure, emptied breast to visit the Way, set aside mat to seek worthies, thickly befriended younger brothers to harmonize kin, clarified rewards and punishments to face those below—heroes exhausted their integrity, claws and fangs gave their lives.

value.assessment: crushed foes, completed prior structure, sought worthies, harmonized younger brothers, clarified rewards; comparable to Chu Zhuang and Qin Mu; later proud, ignored remonstrance, favored monks

units.zh: 取汾、絳，陷許、洛，款僭燕而籓偽蜀，夷隴右而靜河西，俗阜年豐，遠安邇輯，雖楚莊、秦穆何以加焉！
units.en: At his height he held the heartland and the west in prosperity few could match.
units.literal: He took Fen and Jiang, fell Xu and Luo, treated false Yan as vassal and hedged false Shu, leveled Longyou and quieted Hexi—customs rich, years abundant, far quieted and near gathered—though Chu Zhuang or Qin Mu, how could they surpass!

proposals.before: At his height he held the heartland and the west in prosperity few could match.
proposals.after: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo. He won the allegiance of the rival Yan regime and made the regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, the harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those close at hand were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?
proposals.reason: Restore Fen, Jiang, Xu, Luo, Yan, Shu, Longyou, Hexi, prosperous livelihoods, good harvests and unity near and far. The concluding comparison with King Zhuang and Duke Mu belongs here. 藩 means bringing Shu into vassalage.

proposals.before: He took Fen and Jiang, fell Xu and Luo, treated false Yan as vassal and hedged false Shu, leveled Longyou and quieted Hexi—customs rich, years abundant, far quieted and near gathered—though Chu Zhuang or Qin Mu, how could they surpass!
proposals.after: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo. He won the allegiance of the rival Yan regime and made the regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, the harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those close at hand were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?

units.zh: 既而逞志矜功，弗虞後患。
units.en: Then pride undid his caution.
units.literal: Yet afterward he indulged his will and boasted of merit, did not guard against later trouble.

proposals.before: Then pride undid his caution.
proposals.after: Afterward he gave free rein to his ambitions and boasted of his achievements, taking no thought for future trouble.
proposals.reason: Restore indulgence of ambition, boasting of achievement and neglect of future dangers.

value.assessment: crushed foes, completed prior structure, sought worthies, harmonized younger brothers, clarified rewards; comparable to Chu Zhuang and Qin Mu; later proud, ignored remonstrance, favored monks

units.zh: 委涼都於禿髮，授朔方於赫連，專己生災，邊城繼陷，距諫招禍，蕭牆屢發，戰無寧歲，人有危心。
units.en: He entrusted the Liang capital to Tufa and handed Shuofang to Helian, trusting himself bred disaster; border cities fell in succession, rejecting remonstrance invited calamity, inner-wall strife broke out again and again, war had no quiet year, and men lived in fear.
units.literal: He entrusted Liangzhou to Tufa, handed Shuofang to Helian, trusting himself bred disaster; border cities fell in succession, rejecting remonstrance invited calamity; inner walls rose again and again; war without quiet years, men harbored peril in heart.

proposals.before: He entrusted Liangzhou to Tufa, handed Shuofang to Helian, trusting himself bred disaster; border cities fell in succession, rejecting remonstrance invited calamity; inner walls rose again and again; war without quiet years, men harbored peril in heart.
proposals.after: He entrusted the capital of Liang to Tufa and granted Shuofang to Helian. His insistence on having his way bred disasters. Frontier cities fell in succession, and his rejection of remonstrance invited calamity. Trouble repeatedly broke out within his own house. There was no year of respite from warfare, and the people felt themselves in danger.
proposals.reason: 涼都 is the capital of Liang, not the entire Liangzhou; 蕭牆屢發 refers to troubles repeatedly breaking out within the ruling house.

units.zh: 豈宜騁彼雄圖，被深恩於介士；
units.en: He should have showered his soldiers with thanks—
units.literal: How fitting to ride those heroic plans and spread deep favor on armored men—

proposals.before: He should have showered his soldiers with thanks—
proposals.after: With such grand designs to pursue, should he not have shown profound favor to his men-at-arms?
proposals.reason: Retain Xing’s grand ambitions and the favor due to his armored warriors; the rhetorical thought turns to his contrary choice at s0265.

proposals.before: How fitting to ride those heroic plans and spread deep favor on armored men—
proposals.after: With such grand designs to pursue, should he not have shown profound favor to his men-at-arms?
proposals.reason: Retain Xing’s grand ambitions and the favor due to his armored warriors; the rhetorical thought turns to his contrary choice at s0265.

units.zh: 翻崇詭說，加殊禮于桑門！
units.en: —yet he lavished gold on Buddhist monks instead.
units.literal: yet he reversed course to honor crafty doctrine and piled special rites on shaven monks!

proposals.before: —yet he lavished gold on Buddhist monks instead.
proposals.after: Instead he exalted teachings the historian deemed deceptive and paid exceptional honors to Buddhist monks.
proposals.reason: No gold is specified. The historian condemns deceptive teachings and extraordinary honors for Buddhist monks.

value.assessment: crushed foes, completed prior structure, sought worthies, harmonized younger brothers, clarified rewards; comparable to Chu Zhuang and Qin Mu; later proud, ignored remonstrance, favored monks

units.zh: 當有為之時，肄無為之業，麗衣腴食，殆將萬數，析實談空，靡然成俗。
units.en: He let monasteries swell while taxes bled the hills.
units.literal: In a time when action was needed, he practiced non-action's enterprise; gorgeous robes and rich food approached ten thousand; splitting substance they talked emptiness—became custom on the wind.

proposals.before: He let monasteries swell while taxes bled the hills.
proposals.after: At a time that demanded action he devoted himself to the pursuit of nonaction. Those clad in fine robes and fed on rich food numbered nearly ten thousand. Analyzing the real and discoursing on emptiness became the general fashion.
proposals.reason: Restore the antithesis of action and nonaction, the nearly ten thousand richly dressed and fed people, and widespread discussion of the Buddhist doctrine of emptiness. No hillside taxation occurs until s0269.

proposals.reason: Restore the antithesis of action and nonaction, the nearly ten thousand richly dressed and fed people, and widespread discussion of the Buddhist doctrine of emptiness. No hillside taxation occurs until s0269.

units.zh: 夫以漢朝殷廣，猶鄙鴻都之費；
units.en: Even the vast Han court scorned the waste of the Hongdu academy.
units.literal: Even Han's vast abundance still despised Hongdu's expense;

proposals.before: Even the vast Han court scorned the waste of the Hongdu academy.
proposals.after: Even under the wealthy and far-reaching Han dynasty, the expense of the Hongdu academy drew scorn.
proposals.reason: The criticism of spending on Hongdu occurs despite the wealth and extent of the Han; the sentence need not make the Han court itself the critic.

units.zh: 況乎偽境日侵，寧堪永貴之役！
units.en: How much less could a shrinking rebel realm bear endless monastic extravagance?
units.literal: how much more when false borders daily shrank—could it bear eternal costly service!

proposals.before: How much less could a shrinking rebel realm bear endless monastic extravagance?
proposals.after: How, then, could a regime whose borders were daily encroached upon bear the construction work at Yonggui?
proposals.reason: 永貴 is the Yonggui ward, where Xing built a Buddhist stupa (Jinshu 117, 起浮圖於永貴裏). The rhetorical question concerns that specific construction project.

proposals.before: how much more when false borders daily shrank—could it bear eternal costly service!
proposals.after: How, then, could a regime whose borders were daily encroached upon bear the construction work at Yonggui?
proposals.reason: 永貴 is the Yonggui ward, where Xing built a Buddhist stupa (Jinshu 117, 起浮圖於永貴裏). The rhetorical question concerns that specific construction project.

units.zh: 儲用殫竭，山林有稅，政荒威挫，職是之由，坐致淪胥，非天喪也。
units.en: Empty treasuries and forest levies—not fate but policy destroyed Later Qin.
units.literal: Stores were exhausted, hills and forests taxed; government wild, awe broken—this is the reason; sitting to bring ruin—Heaven did not destroy them.

proposals.before: Empty treasuries and forest levies—not fate but policy destroyed Later Qin.
proposals.after: Reserves were exhausted, and even the hills and forests were taxed. Government fell into neglect and authority was broken. These were the causes. They brought ruin upon themselves; Heaven did not destroy them.
proposals.reason: Restore depleted stores, taxation of hills as well as forests, neglected government and loss of authority, which the historian ties to collective downfall.

value.assessment: crushed foes, completed prior structure, sought worthies, harmonized younger brothers, clarified rewards; comparable to Chu Zhuang and Qin Mu; later proud, ignored remonstrance, favored monks

units.zh: 元子以庸懦之質，屬傾擾之餘，內難方殷，外禦斯輟。
units.en: Yao Hong was weak when kin tore the realm apart and Jin struck.
units.literal: Yuanzi with a mediocre and timid substance, amid the aftermath of overturn and turmoil, inner disaster just raging, outer defense then ceased.

proposals.before: Yao Hong was weak when kin tore the realm apart and Jin struck.
proposals.after: Yao Hong, called Yuanzi, was mediocre and timid. He came to power in the aftermath of upheaval, and as internal troubles intensified, defense against outside enemies ceased.
proposals.reason: The focus is Hong’s timidity amid preceding upheavals and the suspension of external defense as internal crises grew. The original does not mention a discrete Jin strike here.

value.assessment: mediocre and timid; inner disaster raging; outer defense ceased; wicked heir lost his plan and surrendered at Zhidao

units.zh: 王師杖順，弭節而下長安；
units.en: Jin marched in righteousness and took Chang'an;
units.literal: The royal army wielded obedience, lowered the pace and descended on Chang'an;

proposals.before: Jin marched in righteousness and took Chang'an;
proposals.after: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.
proposals.reason: 杖順 describes relying on the justice of the cause; 弭節 describes an unhurried advance, and 下長安 the taking of Chang’an.

proposals.before: The royal army wielded obedience, lowered the pace and descended on Chang'an;
proposals.after: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.
proposals.reason: 杖順 describes relying on the justice of the cause; 弭節 describes an unhurried advance, and 下長安 the taking of Chang’an.

units.zh: 凶嗣失圖，系組而降軹道。
units.en: the last heir bound himself at Zhidao.
units.literal: the wicked heir lost his plan, tied cord and surrendered at Zhidao.

proposals.before: the last heir bound himself at Zhidao.
proposals.after: The ill-fated heir had no plan left and surrendered at Zhidao with the cord of submission about his neck.
proposals.reason: Restore the condemned heir’s loss of a plan and actual surrender, with the cord as its sign. The wording evokes the surrender of Qin at Zhidao.

value.assessment: mediocre and timid; inner disaster raging; outer defense ceased; wicked heir lost his plan and surrendered at Zhidao

units.zh: 物極則反，抑斯之謂歟！
units.en: Thus the wheel turns: extremes invite reversal.
units.literal: Things extreme then reverse—does this say it!

units.zh: 贊曰：弋仲剛烈，終表奇節。
units.en: Eulogy: Yao Yizhong was stern and fierce, and in the end displayed remarkable integrity.
units.literal: Eulogy says: Yizhong was stern and fierce, in the end displayed a strange integrity.

value.assessment: stern, fierce, and in the end displayed remarkable integrity

units.zh: 襄實英果，萇惟奸傑。
units.en: Yao Xiang was truly heroic and resolute; Yao Chang was a treacherous champion.
units.literal: Xiang was truly heroic and resolute; Chang alone was a treacherous champion.

proposals.before: Xiang was truly heroic and resolute; Chang alone was a treacherous champion.
proposals.after: Xiang was indeed heroic and resolute; Chang was an outstanding man of treachery.
proposals.reason: 惟 is an emphatic connective introducing Chang’s characterization; it does not say that only Chang was treacherous.

units.zh: 興始崇構，泓遂摧滅。
units.en: Yao Xing first raised the frame; Yao Hong was then destroyed and extinguished.
units.literal: Xing first raised the frame; Hong then was destroyed and extinguished.

proposals.before: Yao Xing first raised the frame; Yao Hong was then destroyed and extinguished.
proposals.after: Under Xing the dynastic edifice rose high; under Hong it came crashing down.
proposals.reason: The paired verse describes the rise and fall of the dynastic structure under Xing and Hong; the object carried forward is the house, rather than Hong’s personal destruction alone.

proposals.before: Xing first raised the frame; Hong then was destroyed and extinguished.
proposals.after: Under Xing the dynastic edifice rose high; under Hong it came crashing down.
proposals.reason: The paired verse describes the rise and fall of the dynastic structure under Xing and Hong; the object carried forward is the house, rather than Hong’s personal destruction alone.

value.assessment: first raised the frame of the state

units.zh: 貽誡將來，無踐危轍。
units.en: Let later ages shun that fatal road.
units.literal: Leave warning to those who come—do not tread this perilous rut.

proposals.before: Let later ages shun that fatal road.
proposals.after: Let this stand as a warning to those who come after: do not follow the same perilous tracks.
proposals.reason: 貽誡 explicitly leaves the preceding history as a warning.
